text: The Dutch power grid is full. Across the Netherlands, more than half of all postcodes are now marked red for new demand. In Liander's area, nearly eight in ten.

For a business, that means no bigger connection. In Amsterdam, eighty-seven requests are waiting, and relief is not expected until twenty twenty-seven. Meanwhile, every fleet is being told to go electric.
Picture a depot with a hundred kilowatt connection, and ten electric trucks. They all roll in at six, and plug in at once. The site pulls a hundred and seventy-eight kilowatts. The fuse blows.
GridFlex fixes that. Without a single new cable.

Enter your postcode, your building, and your fleet. GridFlex builds a charging timetable for every truck. They take turns, using the quiet hours of the night, so the site never crosses its limit, and every truck is full by morning.
But a plan that works on one made-up day proves nothing. So GridFlex tests it on a hundred realistic days it has never seen, and tells you how often it would still go over, by how much, and when.
Then it explains the result in plain language. A person approves or rejects it. GridFlex only recommends. Nothing switches automatically.
Every depot stuck in the queue is a fleet that cannot go electric. GridFlex lets it charge more trucks on the connection it already has. Plan. Stress-test. Explain.
